questions.q: What does the || operator mean on MySQL by default, unlike on Oracle and PostgreSQL?
options: String concatenation, identical to Oracle and PostgreSQL
It is not a legal operator on MySQL at all
Bitwise XOR
Logical OR, not string concatenation
questions.explain: Unless PIPES_AS_CONCAT is explicitly enabled in sql_mode, || means logical OR on MySQL -- CONCAT() is the safe, required choice there instead.

questions.q: What MySQL version is required for the capstone query's CTE and RANK() OVER structure to work without a rewrite?
options: MySQL 5.7 or later
MySQL does not support window functions at all
Any MySQL version, since CTEs have always been supported
MySQL 8.0 or later
questions.explain: MySQL only added CTE and window function support in 8.0 -- earlier versions would need derived subqueries and manual rank calculation instead.

questions.q: Of the three target dialects in this capstone, which one required the fewest changes from the Oracle translation?
options: MySQL
They all required an identical number of changes
PostgreSQL
None of them -- all three needed a full rewrite
questions.explain: PostgreSQL already uses || for concatenation and has long supported CTEs and window functions natively, making it the closest match to the Oracle version and to T-SQL's underlying querying model.

questions.q: What is the real takeaway this capstone demonstrates about the original T-SQL query's join/CTE/window-function structure?
options: It needed zero structural changes across all three target platforms -- only small, specific differences needed attention
Joins are the only part of SQL that is portable across dialects
Window functions could not be translated to any other platform
The entire query had to be rewritten from scratch for every platform
questions.explain: The join graph, GROUP BY, CTE, and window function carried over unchanged in shape across Oracle, MySQL, and PostgreSQL -- only concatenation syntax and one MySQL version gate needed real attention.

questions.q: In the Oracle translation, what replaces T-SQL's 'USE AdventureWorks2012; GO' at the top of the script?
options: A SET SCHEMA statement is always required before every query
An identical USE statement, unchanged
A CREATE DATABASE statement
Nothing -- Oracle connects directly to a schema and has no equivalent statement
questions.explain: Oracle has no USE-equivalent statement for switching databases the way T-SQL does -- a session connects directly to a schema.
